schedule_summary: There are 14 alternating administrations, planned every 14 days after recovery, not 14 pairs. Ifosfamide and etoposide are given on days 1–5 in cycles 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. administration_text: During ifosfamide/etoposide cycles, each medicine is infused over 60 minutes on each of days 1–5. agents.name: Ifosfamide
agents.mechanism: Links genetic strands so cells cannot divide normally
agents.explanation: The liver activates ifosfamide into substances that damage deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Some breakdown products can injure the urinary tract. Mesna and prescribed fluids reduce bladder injury, but do not remove kidney, brain or other chemotherapy risks.
visual: Brain, kidney, urine and blood checks continue
agents.watch: Report confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, marked weakness or seizures immediately. Blood or pain when passing urine, reduced urine, fever or new breathing problems needs urgent review. Continue prescribed mesna and hydration until the team confirms completion.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth/bowel effects, hair loss and fatigue
Brain effects causing confusion, drowsiness, hallucinations or seizures; recovery is not guaranteed
Bladder inflammation or bleeding, kidney filtering/tubular injury and electrolyte losses; kidney damage can persist or appear later
Serious heart or lung injury; allergic reactions
Potentially permanent infertility, later cancers and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.mechanism: Interferes with an enzyme that manages breaks in genetic material
agents.explanation: Etoposide interferes with topoisomerase II, an enzyme that manages breaks in deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Damaged cancer cells cannot divide normally. Blood production and other healthy tissues can also be affected.
visual: Slow infusion and blood-count checks protect safety
agents.watch: Tell the nurse immediately about dizziness, flushing, rash, chest tightness, breathlessness, faintness or infusion-site pain. Contact oncology promptly for fever, bleeding, severe mouth symptoms or a blistering rash.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, appetite loss, mouth soreness and bowel changes
Hair loss and fatigue
Allergic or severe infusion reactions and low blood pressure, particularly with rapid administration
Inflammation or tissue injury at the infusion site, liver effects and severe skin reactions
Later blood cancers, fertility effects and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Vincristine
agents.mechanism: Disrupts the structures needed for cell division
agents.explanation: Vincristine interferes with microtubules, structures needed for cells to divide and for nerves to work normally. This helps explain numbness, weakness and bowel slowing. It is given only into a vein by trained staff; administration into spinal fluid can be fatal.
visual: Cell division and nerves are affected
Bowel and nerve symptoms need early review
agents.watch: Report new numbness, weakness, difficulty walking, jaw pain or hearing/vision changes before another dose. Constipation with pain, vomiting or abdominal swelling, difficulty passing urine, confusion or seizures needs urgent advice. Report infusion-site pain immediately.
risks: Peripheral nerve injury causing tingling, pain, weakness or impaired walking/hand function; effects may persist
Autonomic nerve injury causing severe constipation or bowel paralysis, urinary retention and blood-pressure changes
Low sodium from abnormal water retention, confusion or seizures; hearing, vision or cranial-nerve effects
Hair loss, mouth/bowel symptoms and jaw or muscle pain; blood-count effects can occur in the combination
Allergic reactions, breathing reactions and tissue injury after leakage outside the vein
Fertility and pregnancy harm; wrong-route administration can be fatal

agents.name: Doxorubicin
agents.mechanism: Damages genetic material and disrupts cell division
agents.explanation: Doxorubicin interferes with deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, and the enzymes that manage it. Cancer cells can be damaged, but blood production, the mouth and the heart can also be affected. Previous anthracycline treatment contributes to the heart-risk assessment.
visual: Blood counts and heart function are checked
agents.watch: Report fever, new breathlessness, chest symptoms or palpitations urgently. Tell staff immediately about infusion-site burning or pain. Temporary red urine may reflect the medicine's colour, but visible blood, clots, painful urination or persistent red urine needs assessment.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, vomiting, mouth ulcers, appetite/bowel changes, hair loss and fatigue
Cumulative heart-muscle damage and heart failure, including effects that can appear after treatment; heart-rhythm disturbances
Severe tissue damage if the medicine leaks outside the vein; allergic reactions
Later blood cancers and potentially lasting fertility effects; pregnancy harm

agents.name: Cyclophosphamide
agents.mechanism: Damages genetic material after activation in the body
agents.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is activated into substances that damage deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material. Blood and reproductive cells can also be affected. Urinary breakdown products can injure the bladder, so the prescribed fluid and any mesna plan must be followed.
visual: Urinary metabolites can irritate the bladder
Blood, urine and fluid checks support safety
agents.watch: Report blood or pain when passing urine, reduced urine, fever, new breathlessness, chest symptoms, confusion or severe weakness urgently. Follow the individual fluid plan; do not force large fluid volumes if you have a fluid restriction.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Bladder inflammation or bleeding and kidney/tubular injury
Low blood sodium and excessive water retention, which can cause confusion or seizures
Heart injury, lung inflammation or scarring, and severe liver blood-flow injury
Nausea, vomiting, mouth/bowel effects, hair loss, fatigue and impaired wound healing
Potentially permanent infertility, later cancers and pregnancy harm; allergic reactions

agents.name: Dactinomycin · only if selected for cycles 12 and 14
agents.explanation: This medicine is optional in the final two even-numbered administrations and is included in your consent only if selected. Dactinomycin binds to deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), the cell's genetic material, and disrupts production of ribonucleic acid (RNA), which carries instructions for cell activity. Cancer cells and healthy blood, mouth, gut and liver tissues can be affected.
visual: Genetic instructions cannot be read normally
Blood, liver and infusion-site checks matter
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, severe mouth sores or diarrhoea, jaundice, increasing abdominal pain/swelling or rapid weight gain urgently. Tell staff immediately about infusion-site pain or burning. Report a new painful rash, especially in a previously irradiated area.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding
Mouth and gut ulceration, nausea, vomiting and bowel changes
Severe liver injury, including obstruction of blood flow through small liver vessels
Severe tissue damage if the medicine leaks outside the vein
Increased radiation effects or renewed inflammation in previously irradiated tissue, called radiation recall
Severe skin or allergic reactions, later cancers, fertility effects and pregnancy harm

anatomy: New confusion, unusual sleepiness, hallucinations, unsteadiness or seizures needs urgent assessment.
Report mouth sores or trouble drinking early. Use the prescribed mouth-care and anti-sickness plan.
Report breathlessness, chest pain, swelling or palpitations. Previous anthracycline treatment affects the safe plan.
Blood tests check liver effects. Yellow eyes, dark urine or significant upper abdominal pain needs prompt advice.
Mesna and fluids protect the bladder. Report painful urination, blood or clots, or reduced urine promptly.
Constipation can become severe. Abdominal pain or swelling with vomiting or inability to pass stool needs urgent advice.
Fever, shaking chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding needs immediate oncology contact.
Report numbness, tingling, weakness, walking difficulty, jaw pain or a changed voice before another dose.

monitoring_schedule.note: Safety monitoring is separate from scans and tumour-response review. The exact sequence can change after toxicity or local treatment.

monitoring_test_details.label: Full blood count
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Check infection-fighting cells, anaemia and bleeding risk.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment and each cycle; further samples are directed by symptoms, recovery or the prescribed admission plan.

monitoring_test_details.label: Kidney, liver and electrolytes
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect organ injury and electrolyte loss that affect treatment safety.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Kidney and liver tests at baseline and before every cycle. Sodium, potassium and phosphate at baseline and before each ifosfamide/etoposide cycle; repeat when clinically indicated.

monitoring_test_details.label: Neurological function
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect ifosfamide-related changes in alertness and vincristine nerve toxicity.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Assess alertness and neurological function before every ifosfamide dose. Report numbness, weakness, bowel slowing or walking changes before further vincristine.

monitoring_test_details.label: Urine, fluid balance and weight
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Detect bladder bleeding, kidney effects and fluid retention despite protective treatment.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Check urine for blood before each ifosfamide dose and every 8 hours on treatment days. Staff monitor urine output and fluid balance and weigh daily during the prescribed hydration period.

monitoring_test_details.label: Heart pumping and anthracycline exposure
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess cardiac safety before further doxorubicin.
monitoring_test_details.timing: Before treatment if clinically indicated; repeat when indicated. Heart ultrasound or a pumping scan measures left ventricular ejection fraction; the national source requires greater than 50% for doxorubicin. Review symptoms, previous anthracyclines and radiation exposure before further dosing.

monitoring_test_details.label: Tumour response and local-treatment review
monitoring_test_details.purpose: Assess benefit separately from treatment safety.
monitoring_test_details.timing: The specialist sets scans and clinical reviews according to tumour type, disease extent, symptoms and any surgery or radiotherapy plan.

support.title: Anti-sickness medicines
support.text: Follow one written prevention, home and rescue plan. The team reconciles all steroids and interacting medicines; no generic reference is an additional prescription.

support.title: Mesna and bladder protection
support.text: Ifosfamide cycles: mesna 360 mg/m² intravenously before each dose and at 4 and 8 hours from the START of that dose. It binds bladder-damaging metabolites; it does not prevent every kidney or neurological effect.

support.title: Hydration and fluid balance
support.text: Hospital-prescribed fluids support urine flow and clearance. The team adjusts them to urine output, blood tests, weight and heart/kidney status; continue the prescribed protection after chemotherapy finishes. Follow individual home fluid advice.

support.title: White-cell growth factor
support.text: Required after every administration. After ifosfamide/etoposide: daily injections on days 8–13 (source 0.5 million units/kg, maximum 48 million units/day for primary prevention). After vincristine/cyclophosphamide-containing treatment: pegylated injection 24–48 hours later. These support recovery of infection-fighting cells; fever still needs urgent assessment.

support.title: Mouth and bowel care
support.text: Use the prescribed mouth-care and constipation-prevention plan. Vincristine slows bowel movement through nerve effects; report painful constipation, vomiting or abdominal swelling promptly. Mouth care helps detect and manage damaged lining before drinking becomes difficult.

support.title: Radiotherapy and protective care
support.text: If pelvic radiotherapy is planned, additional mesna is prescribed with cyclophosphamide: 240 mg/m² intravenously before it, then 240 mg/m² intravenously or 480 mg/m² orally 4 and 8 hours from its start. Doxorubicin interruption depends on the radiation field; it is not reintroduced until at least three weeks after radiation ends. Confirm actual dates with both teams.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The treatment service chooses suitable intravenous access. Report burning, pain, swelling or redness during administration immediately. If a port or central catheter is used, agree dressing, flushing, infection precautions and eventual removal arrangements. Do not alter infusion or mesna-pump settings yourself.

support.title: Fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment; these combinations can permanently affect fertility. Obtain a written pregnancy-prevention, contraception and breastfeeding plan covering every medicine and the longest relevant precaution period. Current product instructions differ from the older general six-month regimen paragraph. Do not assume one interval applies to everyone, and contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: For Ewing sarcoma, systemic chemotherapy is combined with surgery and/or radiotherapy for local tumour control. For rhabdomyosarcoma, the specialist combines systemic and local treatment according to site, risk and feasibility. These decisions require the relevant multidisciplinary team; Ewing trial percentages cannot be used as estimates for the other listed tumour types. Rehabilitation, symptom control and psychological support can accompany cancer treatment.

evidence.title: Interval-compressed versus three-weekly chemotherapy in localised Ewing sarcoma
evidence.summary: In a randomised trial of predominantly children and adolescents with localised Ewing sarcoma, giving alternating chemotherapy every two weeks improved event-free survival compared with every three weeks. Longer follow-up of the same study supported sustained benefit. This evidence informs interval choice but does not make the individual national calendars identical to the study.
evidence.intro: In a randomised trial of predominantly children and adolescents with localised Ewing sarcoma, giving alternating chemotherapy every two weeks improved event-free survival compared with every three weeks. Longer follow-up of the same study supported sustained benefit. This evidence informs interval choice but does not make the individual national calendars identical to the study.
evidence.caveat: The trial population was mostly young and had localised Ewing sarcoma. It began with vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide, whereas these national schedules begin with ifosfamide/etoposide; some doses and recovery thresholds also differ. Do not transfer Ewing outcomes to rhabdomyosarcoma, desmoplastic tumours, metastatic disease or every adult. Long-term follow-up is the same cohort, not an independent trial.
evidence.interpretation: The trial population was mostly young and had localised Ewing sarcoma. It began with vincristine/doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide, whereas these national schedules begin with ifosfamide/etoposide; some doses and recovery thresholds also differ. questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Treat cancer throughout the body as part of a specialist plan that also addresses local tumour control. The intended benefit depends on the exact tumour, disease extent and treatment aim. For Ewing sarcoma, systemic chemotherapy is combined with surgery and/or radiotherapy for local tumour control. For rhabdomyosarcoma, the specialist combines systemic and local treatment according to site, risk and feasibility. These decisions require the relevant multidisciplinary team; Ewing trial percentages cannot be used as estimates for the other listed tumour types. Rehabilitation, symptom control and psychological support can accompany cancer treatment.

There are 14 alternating administrations, planned every 14 days after recovery, not 14 pairs. Ifosfamide and etoposide are given on days 1–5 in cycles 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 and 13. Vincristine, doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide are given on day 1 in cycles 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Cycles 12 and 14 contain vincristine and cyclophosphamide with no doxorubicin; dactinomycin may be added only if the consultant selects it. Surgery, radiotherapy, toxicity or delayed recovery may change the sequence or dates.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.

questions.q: Can I restart after symptoms improve?
questions.a: Only after the treating team confirms the new prescription. A normal test or recovered symptom does not erase previous severe toxicity or a permanent-stop decision.

source_provenance.basis: Current official extracted regimen text and specifically retained primary evidence. No original National Cancer Control Programme PDF binary or source-table pixel verification claimed.
source_provenance.clinical_draft_status: Final source-reviewed clinical input hashes pinned; independent clinical/pharmacy approval remains separate.

general: These reusable agent sections do not decide dose, phase, eligibility, prophylaxis or treatment duration. The parent author supplies current National Cancer Control Programme regimen sources and schedule-specific instructions.
No adverse-event percentages are invented or transferred from another cancer population. Generic risks must remain alongside all selected agent sections.
Clinical source hash freeze remains pending. No independent clinical/pharmacy approval, original-PDF binary verification or fresh visual-table review is claimed.
Contraception and breastfeeding instructions must be reconciled across every selected agent and the actual supplied products; do not use the older generic six-month interval as a universal rule.
dactinomycin: Current detailed safety source is the UK manufacturer SmPC, text revision 3 September 2025, EMC update 16 September 2025. It is not proof of current Irish product authorisation or supply.

Historical Irish PA1301/003/001 listing, https://www.hpra.ie/find-a-medicine/for-human-use/authorised-medicines/details/26050, records withdrawal on 1 April 2012 while also displaying Marketed. The old 2011 linked SmPC must not be labelled current Irish information.

This historical licence status does not mean the current National Cancer Control Programme regimen has been withdrawn. Pharmacy must confirm the supplied product and the applicable authorisation/unlicensed-supply arrangements.

UK product advice gives contraception during treatment and at least seven months afterwards for women/four months for men; no breastfeeding. These are agent-specific facts, not an automatically final combined-regimen interval.
cyclophosphamide: Current Irish source is explicitly Cyclophosphamide Seacross 500 mg, revision 7 January 2026; do not silently call it Endoxana or use the older UK Baxter 2016 text as current Irish evidence.
Ewing sarcoma is among the product indications; this does not establish that every tumour or combination in the National Cancer Control Programme source is licensed.
Product renal advice differs from National Cancer Control Programme IE/VAC. No numeric product dose adjustment is imported into patient definitions.
This product states contraception for six months after treatment for women/three months for men; breastfeeding is contraindicated. Reconcile all selected medicines.
vincristine: Current Irish product revision August 2026 specifies female contraception during and at least seven months after treatment; male contraception during and at least four months afterwards; breastfeeding avoidance during and for one month afterwards. Apply the reconciled combined-regimen plan.
CYP3A4/azole interactions can amplify neurotoxicity. The regimen's constipation and interaction plan must accompany the nerve-risk section.
Do not equate vincristine's blood-count effects with the principal marrow toxicity of the whole combination or copy incidence from other combinations.
doxorubicin: The retained HPRA example product was listed as authorised but not marketed when checked; confirm the actual supplied formulation. Conventional doxorubicin must not be substituted with a liposomal formulation.
Temporary red colour does not justify dismissing haematuria in an ifosfamide/cyclophosphamide combination. Lifetime exposure and regimen-specific ceilings remain professional planning issues.
irinotecan: Current October 2025 HPRA retained text supports delayed diarrhoea, weekly blood counts and liver monitoring. A fresh focused fetch was inaccessible; older Irish product text is explicitly supplementary for cholinergic/lung warnings, not dosing.

Early cholinergic symptoms and delayed diarrhoea are separate. Atropine glaucoma precautions and the prescribed loperamide/escalation plan belong in regimen support; no adult self-dosing schedule is supplied here.
Do not import colorectal doses, paediatric eligibility or numerical adverse-event rates into the sarcoma combinations.
temozolomide: EMA index lists product information updated 18 August 2026. One direct PDF attempt returned HTTP 429; no identical retry was made. Indexed official safety sections and readable manufacturer text were used; full latest-table inspection is not claimed.
Do not transfer glioma/radiotherapy seizure or neurological event rates, glioma dosing, or a 42-day radiotherapy monitoring calendar to these sarcoma regimens.

The National Cancer Control Programme 00504 and 00757 sources themselves require Pneumocystis prophylaxis: this is not an extrapolated requirement based only on the brain-radiotherapy product schedule.
The current product recommends liver tests after each cycle and warns of delayed hepatotoxicity. Baseline-only or pre-cycle-only wording would be incomplete.

consent_generic_risks: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste changes, diarrhoea or constipation; fatigue, hair, nail and skin changes; changes in sexual wellbeing; allergic reactions and intravenous-line complications; blood clots, including clots in the legs or lungs; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. The likelihood and severity differ between medicines, doses and people. Read this general section together with the risks of every medicine actually included in the agreed treatment phase.
